profile.name: Hearth Home Appliances
profile.summary: US maker of kitchen and laundry appliances (~2,000 employees, factories in Tennessee and Ohio). Sells refrigerators, dishwashers, washing machines and microwaves through big-box stores and its own website. Imports some parts from Mexico and Asia. No food, no medicine, no vehicles.
businessLines: Retail and online sales with product warranties
applies: DOE energy and water efficiency standards for home appliances
Consumer product safety rules and recalls (CPSC)
EPA rules on refrigerants and chemicals in products
Tariffs and trade rules on imported appliance parts
Factory workplace safety (OSHA) and labor rules
doesNotApply: Food, drugs, medical devices, aviation, banking
Energy rules for power plants, pipelines or utilities

product-standards.description: Energy efficiency, product safety, recalls, refrigerants

prompts.jevQuestion: Would the general counsel of this company need to know about this federal document because it could create, change or remove a compliance obligation or material legal risk for the company's actual business lines? Routine filings for other industries are not relevant.
prompts.extractSystem: Extract every dated obligation or deadline (comment due, effective, compliance) stated in the text. Quote the sentence verbatim. If none, return an empty list.
prompts.actionsSystem: Write one action item per document for a busy general counsel: an imperative sentence (≤ 25 words) saying what the owner should do and why, in plain English a non-lawyer understands — spell out acronyms, no regulatory jargon. Do NOT write any dates or citations — those are rendered separately from verified data.
prompts.webLeadsSystem: You find leads on new US federal regulatory actions. Search, then list the URLs you found. Do not summarise law from memory.
prompts.webLeadsPrompt:
{{profile}}

Find US federal regulatory developments (final rules, proposed rules, guidance, enforcement) published {{windowStart}} to {{windowEnd}} that could affect this company. Run at most 3 searches. Reply with the URLs only.
prompts.panelJudge:
You are one judge on a panel grading action items that a General Counsel would forward to a colleague.
For EVERY item and EVERY listed criterion, answer PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN (UNKNOWN only if the item gives you too little to decide), with a one-line reason.
Judge only the criterion asked. Do not judge whether the rule is truly relevant to the company — that is graded elsewhere.
Each item is a card as the reader sees it: the action text plus "datesShown" (verified dates displayed next to the action) and "tier". Action texts deliberately contain no dates, so a date the rubric mentions counts as covered when it appears in "datesShown".
For "covers", a paraphrase that conveys the business-relevant substance counts; exact names, populations and sub-details are not required.

Criteria:
{{criteria}}

Items (a "rubric" is present only when the answer key has one for that item):
{{items}}

Abstract: The Criminal Law Technical Amendments Act of 2002 ("Technical Amendments Act") became law on November 2, 2002, as part of the 21st Century Department of Justice Appropriations Authorization Act. The Technical Amendments Act amended sections 401(d), 402(c), and 403 of the Controlled Substances Act by replacing outmoded fine amounts with a reference to title 18 of the United States Code in each place that a specific fine amount had appeared. In this rulemaking, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is amending its regulations to conform them to the statutory amendments made to the Controlled Substances Act by the Technical Amendments Act.

Title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (26-7)
Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: EPA is proposing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. Once finalized, the SNURs would require persons who intend to manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or process any of these chemical substances for an activity that is proposed as a significant new use by this rulemaking to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing that activity. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification, made an appropriate determination regarding that notification, and taken such actions as required by that determination.

[2026-22383] Proposed Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
Action: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
Abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-25-09, which applies to certain The Boeing Company Model 757 airplanes. AD 2024-25-09 requires installing new relays and changing certain wire bundles leading to the power transfer unit (PTU) control valve. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-25-09, the FAA determined that the requirements bulletin mandated by AD 2024-25-09 contains errors. In some cases, those errors prevent the actions required by AD 2024-25-09 from being fully accomplished. In other cases, the errors would allow actions that could introduce new hazards affecting the operation and thus the availability of the PTU. This proposed AD would require, depending on the airplane configuration, installing new relays and new connectors, changing certain wire bundles, doing an operational test, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

Title: Scotts Valley Band of Pomo Indians of California Liquor Control Ordinance; Correction
Action: Notice; correction.
Abstract: This notice publishes several corrections to the Scotts Valley Band of Pomo Indians of California Liquor Control Ordinance, as amended, published on June 1, 2026. The Tribe requested that the Bureau of Indian Affairs make three corrections to typographical errors it identified in its original Ordinance submission that was previously published in the Federal Register. First, Article I, Section 3 mistakenly identifies the Tribe's trust land as being in "Vallejo County"; the correct geographic description is "the City of Vallejo, Solano County, California." Second, Article I, Section 3(v) incorrectly uses the term "Indian county" instead of the correct statutory term "Indian country" as used in 18 U.S.C. 1154 and 1161. Third, Article VII, Section 1 contains a typographical error referring to "uncontested suits or actions"; the correct phrase is "unconsented suits or actions," accurately reflecting the Tribe's intent to preserve its sovereign immunity.

Abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Costruzioni Aeronautiche Tecnam S.P.A. (Tecnam) Model P2006T airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of damage on the engine mount structure caused by defective non-conforming engine shock mounts being installed. This proposed AD would require inspecting for the installation of non-conforming engine shock mounts and replacing any non-conforming engine shock mount with an approved part. This proposed AD would also prohibit installation of a non-conforming engine shock mount on any airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

[2026-22679] Rule — Agriculture Department; Food and Nutrition Administration
Title: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC): Online Ordering and Transactions and Food Delivery Revisions To Meet the Needs of a Modern, Data-Driven Program
Action: Final rule with request for comment.
Abstract: This final rule considers public comments submitted in response to the proposed rule to remove barriers to online ordering and internet-based transactions in the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) published on February 23, 2023. USDA FNA is issuing this regulatory action to support State innovation and develop and implement modernized systems, while underscoring program integrity. It allows for the use of new technologies to improve the WIC shopping experience while increasing access to healthy foods for WIC participants. This final rule also complements the Program's complete transition to electronic benefit transfer (EBT) by streamlining and modernizing certain WIC food delivery regulations to support current technology and future innovation, and introduces measures to support a modern, data-driven program that uses new technologies for food delivery.

[2026-22682] Rule — Interior Department; Fish and Wildlife Service
Title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Technical Corrections for 43 Wildlife and Plant Species on the Lists of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants
Action: Direct final rule.
Abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), announce technical corrections for 43 wildlife and plant species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). For 7 wildlife species and 30 plant species that predominately occur in California and Nevada, we are revising the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and the List of Endangered and Threatened Plants ("the Lists") to reflect the current scientifically accepted taxonomy and nomenclature of these species. We are also making commensurate revisions to the applicable critical habitat sections. Further, for six wildlife species occurring within the United States and territories, we are correcting errors in the Lists made in previous publications. The taxonomic, nomenclatural, and orthographic revisions and the corrections of publication errors are editorial in nature and involve no substantive changes to the Lists or any applicable regulations.

[2026-22695] Proposed Rule — Commerce Department; National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
Title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Amendment 128 to the FMP for Groundfish of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area and Amendment 116 to the FMP for the Groundfish Fisheries of the Gulf of Alaska; Small Sablefish Release
Action: Notice of availability; request for comments.
Abstract: The North Pacific Fishery Management Council (Council) submitted amendment 128 to the Fishery Management Plan (FMP) for Groundfish of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area (BSAI FMP) and amendment 116 to the FMP for Groundfish fisheries of the Gulf of Alaska (GOA FMP) to the Secretary of Commerce for review. If approved, these amendments would increase operational flexibility to allow vessels fishing for sablefish with fixed gear under the Individual Fishing Quota (IFQ) Program or Western Alaska Community Development (CDQ) Program to release sablefish and would revise the annual allocation process to account for sablefish discards. This action is intended to promote the goals and objectives of the Magnuson- Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act), the BSAI and GOA FMPs, and other applicable laws.

Title: Specific Listing for 3-Chloromethcathinone, A Currently Controlled Schedule I Substance
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is establishing a specific listing and DEA Controlled Substances Code Number (drug code) for 1-(3-chlorophenyl)-2-(methylamino)propan-1-one (3- chloromethcathinone; 3-CMC) in schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). Although 3-chloromethcathinone is not specifically listed in schedule I of the CSA with its own unique drug code, it is a schedule I controlled substances in the United States because it is a positional isomer of 4-chloromethcathinone, which is a schedule I hallucinogen. Therefore, DEA is simply amending the schedule I hallucinogenic substances list in its regulations to separately include 3- chloromethcathinone.
